messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: partial explanation of strangeness
parts:
I figured out part of the reason why there's so much more variance for
the rats example than there was before: it's due to a change of
variable.

Specifically, Bob recoded the example so that we're running nuts on*
deviations, not variances. I guess this makes the problem geometry a
little harder for nuts/hmc, since it makes burn-in take longer, which
increases the variance of the step size epsilon. It looks like the
fast runs are situations where it doesn't actually burn in completely
in 1000 iterations, which is bad.

Matt

* Going nuts on? Makes me wish we had an algorithm called AMOK.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] partial explanation of strangeness
parts:
I didn't mean to change the model. But I did
mean to make the reported parameters the deviations.

You can have it either way. I changed what Matt had as:

------------------------
parameters {
double(0,) sigma_sq;
}
derived parameters {
double(0,) sigma;
sigma <- sqrt(sigma_sq);
}
---------------------

to:

--------------------------
parameters {
double(0,) sigma;
}
derived parameters {
double(0,) sigma_sq;
sigma_sq <- square(sigma);
}
-----------------------

In both cases, the prior was based on variance and the
normal itself based on deviation (that's how it's parameterized
in Stan):

--------------------
model {
sigma_sq ~ inv_gamma(0.001,0.001);
y ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}
--------------------

Does this really change the geometry so much as to
make it much harder to tune? If so, this will be
a blessing and a curse when it comes to tuning model
code to be more efficient.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] partial explanation of strangeness
parts:
The model's the same, it's just that the space that we're simulating
the dynamics in is a little warped from where it was. I found that
with the original specification it always worked fine and found an
epsilon that's within a pretty tight range, whereas with the new
specification it was much more variable and sometimes didn't quite
converge.

It's weird, and a little unsettling, but I guess it shouldn't be that
surprising.

Incidentally, I think this problem would probably disappear if we were
a little smarter about how we initialize.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] partial explanation of strangeness
parts:
Hmm. We are. Oops. So "warp" wasn't the appropriate word, so much as
"stretch." And the explanation's actually a little simpler蓉sing sd
instead of var means that the variance parameters are stretched out by
a factor of two, and that must make the scaling even worse. The good
news is that this should be easily fixed by diagonal rescaling.

Matt
